headline: One point apart, and a night for Eric Roy
summary: Friday's Ligue 1 game at Brest is also a tribute to Eric Roy, the coach both clubs shared. The match itself is close: only 1 point separates them in mid-table. Brest's case is their home form, a 5-1 win over Angers this month. Nice lost 1-2 at Lyon on Sunday, where Keito Nakamura was sent off. Brest are without defender Raphaël Le Guen, who had played all 450 league minutes. Across 10 bookmakers, margin removed, Brest are 42.2% favourites, but rated only 0.25 goals better, with the goal line at 2.75. A tight evening, and the draw stays live.
read: Brest are narrow home favourites, rated only a quarter of a goal better than a Nice side that has lost both of its away games in the last five. With one point between them in mid-table and 2.75 goals the market's 50/50 line, this profiles as a tight game in which the draw is a live outcome.

facts.fact: Brest are the market's favourites at 42.2% to win, against Nice's 29.0%.
facts.meaning: A home win is the most likely single result but far from a certainty — Nice's chance sits roughly level with the draw.

facts.fact: The handicap fair line is -0.25 goals, so Brest are rated only a quarter of a goal better than Nice.
facts.meaning: That is a near-even rating — the market expects a tight game in which the draw stays live.

facts.fact: Only one point separates them: Brest are 10th on 9 points, Nice 13th on 8, both after seven matches.
facts.meaning: Friday's winner moves above the other — a direct mid-table swing rather than a routine fixture.

facts.fact: Brest created 3.82 expected goals in their 5-1 home win over Angers on 10 October.
facts.meaning: At home Brest turn territory into real chances — that is the football case for their favouritism.

facts.fact: Nice lost 2-1 at Lyon on Sunday, a stoppage-time Wahi equaliser ruled out for centimetres.
facts.meaning: They arrive off a defeat, three losses in seven, and below Brest in the table.

facts.fact: Keito Nakamura was sent off in the 70th minute at Lyon, the outlet saying the red card cost Nice dear.
facts.meaning: Nice could be without their wide man through suspension, thinning the attacking options on Friday.

facts.fact: Brest are without defender Raphaël Le Guen, who had played all 450 league minutes this season, after a broken leg.
facts.meaning: A settled starter gone from the back line for a game where the draw is very much in play.

facts.fact: Nice's absentee list runs to five names, but the minutes are thin: Mendy has 124 this season, Sanson three.
facts.meaning: The missing men are fringe rather than first choice, so the side that lost at Lyon is largely the one that travels.

sources.fact: Julien Lachuer said only Brendan Chardonnet and Raphaël Le Guen should miss the visit of Nice through injury.
Giovani Versini stopped training on Wednesday and is doubtful for Nice, though his coach Julien Lachuer has not fully ruled him out of the squad.
Versini returned to training and Baldé is said to be reassuring ahead of the Nice match.
Olivier Pantaloni wants to neutralise Brest striker Ludovic Ajorque, whose statistics are highlighted as a threat.
Brest drew 1-1 at Lille on Saturday, again pairing Gautier Lloris and Lucas Tousart in central defence.
Brest were sanctioned by the LFP disciplinary commission on Wednesday 21 October, with the details of the sanction listed by the outlet.
Nice lost 2-1 at Lyon on Sunday in Ligue 1's 7th round and remain 13th in the table.
Nice had a goal by Wahi ruled out for a matter of centimetres in stoppage time at Lyon.
